- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — cap forecast peak and introduce mild downward slope.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to 0.3), model tends to overestimate — reduce forecast by 1-2% relative to recent mean.
- Model consistently underestimates true values when sentiment is positive and price is trending upward — increase forecast by 1-3% for such regimes.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in response to sentiment shifts — delay correction by 1-2 days if sentiment turns sharply.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to underestimate lows — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for 3-5 day lows.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — smooth sentiment influence over 3-5 day window before adjusting forecast.
